title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: makers can build declarative agents with flexible layouts and rich UX components
summary: The roadmap facts and the documented agent controls are supported, including preview automation for User access. The licensing statements conflict: the briefing correctly identifies an included Microsoft 365 Copilot entitlement but also tells readers that no licence has been published. Narrow those statements to the unpublished requirements specific to the planned layouts.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Governance controls; Why it matters
claims.claim: Blocking restricts organization-wide access to the selected agent.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. ... Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects Microsoft Copilot and other hosts such as Outlook and Teams.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products

claims.claim: Blocking agents created with SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry affects only availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access reaches the user access control.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: All users is the default User access option.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls; Why it matters
claims.claim: User access controls which organization members can access and install agents and plugins, including specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Use User access to control how members of your organization access and install agents and plugins. ... Specific users or groups - This option lets you select specific users or groups in your organization to have access to agents and plugins.

claims.quote: This article lists the Agent resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta. These resources also support remediation and applyOnce.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the documented role for the signed-in user applying the Agent resource baseline.

claims.claim: An active applyOnce monitor applies its baseline in a background job on behalf of the signed-in administrator.

claims.claim: An active applyOnce monitor becomes inactive after its background run.
claims.quote: An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive. Its result reports the outcome of the run.

claims.claim: The documented Block and User access controls govern agent availability and access rather than separately switching layouts or components.
claims.quote: Use User access to control how members of your organization access and install agents and plugins. Plugins include tools, MCP servers, connectors, skills, and other AI artifacts.
